title: A fuzzer for a request parser
description:
Throw random input at a request parser to find crashes before user mode does.

```
seed 1: 100000 inputs, 0 crashes, 3 rejected kinds: size, version, count
found: count * 16 overflowed the length check -> fixed
```
hints: `count * 16` can overflow a 32-bit number and pass a check it should fail; check `count <= (length - 12) / 16` instead (lesson 5.02).
Mutating a valid buffer (flip a byte, change the count) finds more bugs than pure random bytes.
requirements: A parser for `{ size, version, count, entries[count] }` where each entry is 16 bytes.
Generate random buffers with `std::mt19937`, mostly near-valid (mutate a good one), and call the parser.
The parser must never read outside the buffer: check with an explicit bounds-checked reader.
stretch: Keep the inputs that reached new code (count which checks they hit) and mutate those: a tiny coverage-guided fuzzer.
